rows.head: A natural hat trick for Thompson
rows.story: This one got way too interesting for the Sabres. There were six goals in the first period alone. Mikael Granlund and Cutter Gauthier scored power-play goals 57 seconds apart early in the period to put the Ducks up 2-0.
rows.calls: Zero of two preview calls held

rows.head: Schaefer plays hero in overtime
rows.story: Joel Eriksson Ek got the scoring started for the Wild just 27 seconds into the game. The Islanders’ Ryan Pulock left early in the first period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with an upper-body injury.
rows.calls: One of three preview calls held

rows.head: Cooley lights the lamp for a hat trick
rows.story: Logan Cooley got the scoring started for the Mammoth early in the first, and he struck again midway through the period to make it 2-0. Erik Karlsson got the Penguins on the board midway through the second. Rickard Rakell tied it up shorthanded midway through the third, and Ben Kindel put the Pens ahead 3-2 with 25 seconds left.

rows.head: The Kings blow a four-goal lead, then win it in overtime
rows.story: Tyler Kleven opened the scoring for the Senators midway through the first. Erik Haula made it 1-1 for Los Angeles on the power play less than four minutes later. The second period belonged to the Kings.

rows.head: Smith’s two goals spark the Sharks
rows.story: Filip Bystedt played his first NHL game. Drew O'Connor got the scoring started for the Canucks midway through the first. Liam Öhgren made it 2-0 late in the second, and that was all they would get.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: The Lightning survive a scare
rows.story: This one got way too interesting for the Lightning. Neal Pionk, who scores in about 1 game in 12, scored twice. Brayden Point got the scoring started for the Lightning early in the first, but Pionk tied it up for Winnipeg late in the period, in his 600th NHL game.
rows.calls: Two of three preview calls held

rows.head: Arvidsson lights the lamp for a hat trick
rows.story: Connor Bedard opened the scoring for the Blackhawks early in the first, and that was all they would get. Viktor Arvidsson made it 1-1 for Detroit early in the second. John Gibson stopped Frank Nazar on a penalty shot midway through the period.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Hutson has two goals as the Capitals get past the Predators
rows.story: Filip Forsberg opened the scoring for the Predators on the power play midway through the first, but Cole Hutson tied it 1-1 for Washington three and a half minutes later. Boone Jenner put the Capitals up 2-1 early in the second. Forsberg struck again just under five minutes later to tie it 2-2.
rows.calls: Three of four preview calls held

rows.head: Kochetkov wins his first nine, a Hurricanes record
rows.story: Jordan Martinook struck first for the Hurricanes late in the first, and Logan Stankoven made it 2-0 early in the second. Mark Jankowski stretched the lead to 3-0 just 16 seconds into the third, and that one stood up as the winner. Denton Mateychuk and Kent Johnson scored just under three minutes apart early in the period to cut Carolina’s lead to 3-2, but the Hurricanes held on.
rows.calls: One of four preview calls held

rows.head: Caufield has two goals as the Canadiens take down the Stars
rows.story: It was a busy first period. Cole Caufield got the scoring started for the Canadiens early in the period, but Wyatt Johnston made it 1-1 for Dallas on the power play midway through the period. Alex Newhook and Caufield scored 27 seconds apart late in the period to put the Habs up 3-1.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Thomas has a goal and two assists as the Blues take down the Bruins
rows.story: James Hagens got the scoring started for the Bruins early in the first, but they didn’t score again. Jimmy Snuggerud tied it up for St. Louis on the power play late in the period, and Philip Broberg gave the Blues the lead early in the second.

rows.head: Lundell lights the lamp for a hat trick
rows.story: Bokondji Imama and Tyrel Bauer dropped the gloves early in the first, and Sam Reinhart struck first for the Panthers on the power play late in the period. Anton Lundell stretched the lead to 2-0 early in the second. Winnipeg had a goal taken off on a challenge early in the period.

rows.head: Jack Hughes has two goals as the Devils beat the Golden Knights
rows.story: It was a busy first period. Luke Hughes got the scoring started for the Devils early in the period. Mark Stone and Ivan Barbashev scored a minute and a half apart late in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead, and that was all they would get.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Four points for Coronato as the Flames beat the Kraken
rows.story: Adam Klapka and Curtis Douglas squared off early in the first. Morgan Frost got the scoring started for the Flames on the power play early in the period. Frédérick Gaudreau tied it 1-1 for Seattle midway through the period.
rows.calls: Two of four preview calls held

rows.head: Faulk meets his old team
rows.story: The Red Wings have won two in a row, and the Blues (6-6-1) beat Boston 4-1 on Thursday. Going in, the Blues are fifth in the Central (tied for 22nd in the NHL) and the Wings last in the Atlantic (tied for 16th). The Blues have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .588, and their finishing has held them back.

rows.head: Blueger returns to Vancouver
rows.story: The Maple Leafs (7-6-2) lost 5-4 to Seattle on Wednesday, and the Canucks (3-11-1) lost 3-2 to San Jose on Thursday. Going in, the Maple Leafs are sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 13th in the NHL) and the Canucks are last in the NHL. The Maple Leafs’ record (.533) is about what their chances are worth.

rows.head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
rows.story: The Islanders have won two in a row, and the Oilers (9-2-2) beat Calgary 4-0 on Wednesday. Going in, the Oilers are first in the Pacific (third in the NHL) and the Islanders fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 13th). The Oilers’ record (.769) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.622), largely thanks to their finishing.

rows.note: Stars PP vs. Blue Jackets PK
rows.head: The Stars’ power play has a target
rows.story: The Blue Jackets (5-6-0) lost 3-2 to Carolina on Thursday, and the Stars (7-5-1) lost 5-2 to Montréal the same night. Going in, the Jackets are seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Stars fourth in the Central (tied for 16th). The Blue Jackets get their defensemen shooting (5th) and get a lot of their shots blocked (29th).

rows.head: Fresh legs vs. Tired ones
rows.story: The Avalanche won the teams’ first meeting this season, 7-3 in Calgary on Oct 8. The Flames (6-7-0) beat Seattle 6-2 last night, and the Avalanche (7-5-1) beat New Jersey 5-2 on Wednesday. Going in, the Flames are fifth in the Pacific (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Avalanche third in the Central (tied for 16th).

rows.head: The Bruins hunt better looks than the Blackhawks
rows.story: The Blackhawks (4-9-0) lost 4-1 to Detroit on Thursday, and the Bruins (9-4-1) lost 4-1 to St. Louis the same night. Going in, the Hawks are last in the Central (31st in the NHL) and the Bruins first in the Atlantic (tied for fourth).

rows.head: The Senators should drive the play
rows.story: The Sharks won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-2 in Ottawa on Oct 22. The Senators (8-5-1) lost 6-5 in overtime to Los Angeles on Thursday, while the Sharks (7-6-1) beat Vancouver 3-2 the same night. Going in, the Sens are fifth in the Atlantic (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Sharks fourth in the Pacific (tied for 16th).

rows.head: Panarin’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The Kings (4-6-2) beat Ottawa 6-5 in overtime on Thursday, and the Sabres have won two in a row. Going in, the Sabres are seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Kings seventh in the Pacific (tied for 28th). The Sabres’ record (.577) is about what their chances are worth.

rows.head: The Canadiens are on a heater
rows.story: The Penguins won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-5 in overtime in Pittsburgh on Oct 3. The Canadiens have won four straight, while the Pens (5-6-2) lost 4-3 in overtime to Utah on Thursday. Going in, the Penguins are sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Canadiens second in the Atlantic (tied for sixth).

rows.head: The Lightning are going to let it fly
rows.story: The Lightning (8-3-1) beat Winnipeg 6-4 on Thursday, while the Predators (4-4-5) lost 4-3 to Washington the same night. Going in, the Lightning are fourth in the Atlantic (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Predators sixth in the Central (tied for 22nd). The Lightning get into more chippy games than anyone (1st), rarely ice the puck (2nd) and keep shots away from their net (3rd).

rows.head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
rows.story: The Rangers are on a three-game losing streak, while the Oilers (9-2-2) beat Calgary 4-0 on Wednesday. The Oil played last night, and the Rangers are rested. Going in, the Oilers are first in the Pacific (third in the NHL) and the Rangers fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 16th).

rows.head: The Jets need a win
rows.story: The Jets are winless in eight (0-6-2), while Carolina has won three straight. The Hurricanes won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in Winnipeg on Oct 17. Going in, the Jets are seventh in the Central (tied for 26th in the NHL) and the Canes are first in the NHL.

rows.head: Unstoppable force vs. Immovable object
rows.story: The Capitals have won three straight, while the Wild (9-3-3) lost 4-3 in overtime to the Islanders on Thursday. Going in, the Wild are first in the Central (second in the NHL) and the Capitals third in the Metropolitan (tied for 13th). The Wild’s record (.700) is about what their chances are worth.

rows.head: Jensen meets his old team
rows.story: The Senators (8-5-1) lost 6-5 in overtime to Los Angeles on Thursday, and the Ducks (5-7-1) lost 7-6 to Buffalo the same night. The Senators played last night, and the Ducks are rested. Going in, the Sens are fifth in the Atlantic (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Ducks sixth in the Pacific (tied for 26th).

rows.head: Who drives the play: the Mammoth
rows.story: The Flyers are winless in three (0-2-1), while the Mammoth (9-5-0) beat Pittsburgh 4-3 in overtime on Thursday. Going in, the Mammoth are second in the Central (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Flyers last in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th). The Mammoth have played better than their record (.643) says: their chances are worth about .737, and their goaltending has held them back.

rows.note: Red Wings PP vs. Panthers PK
rows.head: DeBrincat’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The Panthers have won three straight, and the Red Wings have won two in a row. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Red Wings last (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Panthers third (tied for sixth). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

rows.head: The Avalanche should tilt the ice
rows.story: The Avalanche (7-5-1) beat New Jersey 5-2 on Wednesday, while the Blackhawks (4-9-0) lost 4-1 to Detroit on Thursday. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Avalanche third (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Blackhawks last (31st). The Avalanche’s record (.577) is about what their chances are worth.

rows.head: Marner’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The Golden Knights (9-5-1) lost 5-2 to New Jersey on Friday, and the Bruins (9-4-1) lost 4-1 to St. Louis on Thursday. Going in, the Knights are second in the Pacific (tied for fourth in the NHL) and the Bruins first in the Atlantic (tied for fourth).

rows.head: The Flames are going to let it fly
rows.story: The Flames (6-7-0) beat Seattle 6-2 on Friday, and the Sharks (7-6-1) beat Vancouver 3-2 on Thursday. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Flames fifth (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Sharks fourth (tied for 16th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

standout.sub: Tied for the most by anyone in one game this season.
